phases.fact: Actor A and Actor B previously entered an economic arrangement concerning Territory M.
Actor A intervened inside Territory M during an internal disturbance.
Actor C acted in Territory M without consulting Actor A after interpreting Actor A's prior external relations as relevant to its own position.
Actor B interpreted Actor C's action as part of a wider coordination and deployed a state vessel into Territory M.
Actor D made a public signal directed at Actor B during the developing dispute.
Actors A and B continued direct negotiations while Actor C sought participation in the discussion.
Actors A and B concluded a settlement that altered their formal positions and exchanged territorial concessions.
